name: אינטגרל מסוים בהצבה – t·(t²−a)ⁿ, רמז u=t²−a (באנגלית)
questiontext:
Evaluate the following definite integral:

Hint: Use the substitution \(u = {{CT:0}}\)

\( \displaystyle \int^{{CT:1}}_{{CT:2}} {{CT:3}}\,d{{CT:4}} = \) [[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: First find an antiderivative by the substitution, then evaluate it at the two limits and subtract.
Step 1 — The substitution

We need to solve

\[ \int {{CT:3}} d{{CT:4}} \]

using the substitution \(u = {{CT:0}}\).

Substitution: \( \int f(g(x))\,g'(x)\,dx=\int f(u)\,du,\ u=g(x) \)

So, if \(u = {{CT:0}}\), then \(d{{CT:5}} = {{CT:6}}d{{CT:4}}\), and so \(d{{CT:4}} = \frac{d{{CT:5}}}{{CT:6}}\).

Step 2 — An antiderivative

Hence,

\[ \begin{aligned} \int {{CT:3}} d{{CT:4}} &= \int {{CT:7}} \frac{d{{CT:5}}}{{CT:6}} \\ &= \int {{CT:8}} d{{CT:5}} \\ &= {{CT:9}}+c \\ &= {{CT:10}} \end{aligned} \]

Step 3 — The definite integral

We need

\[ \int^{{CT:1}}_{{CT:2}} {{CT:3}} d{{CT:4}} \]

so, recall that if \(\int f(x) dx = F(x)+c\) then \(\int^a_b f(x) dx = F(a) - F(b).\) So, let

\[ F({{CT:4}}) = {{CT:11}} \]

Then,

\[ \begin{aligned} \int^{{CT:1}}_{{CT:2}} {{CT:3}} d{{CT:4}} &= F({{CT:1}}) - F({{CT:2}}) \\ &= {{CT:12}}-\left({{CT:13}}\right) \\ &= {{CT:14}} \end{aligned} \]

on_true.feedback: This is a definite integration problem, so your answer should be a number. This is the correct integral, but you have not evaluated it.
